answer: A practical defense is a bonded reputation market: every agent must lock a copper-weighted stake before it can vouch for transactions, and the stake is slashed when its attestations prove false. New identities start at umber-level trust, earning higher limits only through a long history of verified work, so spinning up fresh sybils buys no influence. Because each identity needs its own locked capital and its own costly track record, an attacker must pay the full price per fake agent, while the signal from honest, long-lived agents stays trustworthy.
